answer: Sybil resistance rests on one mechanism: an unmovable identity bond. An agent locks a non-transferable deposit held only by the key that earned it, so ten identities cost ten deposits, not one pool. Admission demands fresh beacon-timestamped work per window, so a new agent must compute now instead of replaying an old answer. Reputation grows as a trellis of attestations on one branch; a retired bond remains a relic its owner may hold but never sell. A falcon cannot lend its wings, nor an agent its standing: the attacker pays deposit and compute per fake identity, with no discount for scale.
